speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) in the past 10 years, how many HDB BTO applicants who purchased their flat as fiancé and fiancée, did not submit their marriage certificate when requested for verification after six months of collecting their keys; (b) how many of such applicants have refused to surrender their flats when informed, resulting in HDB taking recovery action; and (c) how many have managed to find a replacement who are eligible as joint applicants to retain the flat as approved by HDB.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The three-month period is generally sufficient as most couples would have ample time after the flat application to plan for their marriage.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Should the couple require more time due to unexpected circumstances, HDB may grant a further three-month extension and exercise flexibility on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Some of these applicants were granted further extensions of time due to extenuating circumstances and were able to submit their marriage certificate subsequently.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Couples who do not intend to proceed with their marriage would have to surrender their flat to HDB.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In some cases, an exception can be made to have one of the applicants retain the flat with the inclusion of a family member originally listed in the application, with the agreement of the other party.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Owners who refuse to regularise their lease will face compulsory acquisition actions by HDB.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The remainder are recent cases, where many had cited difficulties proceeding with their marriage during the COVID-19 period.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I am wondering if you could just elaborate a little bit on the reason why the stipulation that an original member of the application has to be included.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I say this because I have had residents that have made a request because they no longer ended up with the original intended partner, actually try to apply with another new partner – and all the parties involved agreed with the process – but because, of course, the new partner is not listed in the original application, this was rejected.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Hence, the retention of the flat is not allowed and the flat is to be surrendered to HDB.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because with the other family member, they would have qualified on their own even without marriage.
